tasks.task: Find the biggest drop-off in a sign-up or checkout funnel

items.when: When you have exported events or step counts and need each step defined, counted and ranked by loss
When the client only has weekly or monthly counts per step and wants the biggest drop named
When you have a raw event log and also need time to convert between steps
When the funnel runs from first visit to day 30, to confirm the leak and the missing first-visit step
When step counts are split by join week, to see which change moved which rate and if the report holds
When every step looks leaky and you must pick the one that limits growth

tasks.task: Build a retention cohort table by start month

items.when: When you have sign-up and activity or cancel dates and must agree the start, return and period first
When the client pastes a simple export and wants to see who stays after one, three and six months
When the owner needs the grid as a colour-coded picture with a plain reading
When you want retention curves by group and feature use to compare against the grid
Before you share the grid, to check the method, the sums and small cohorts read as trends

tasks.task: Write or repair a product tracking plan

items.when: When you need each event named, timed and typed, starting from the questions it must answer
When a launch or redesign is coming and the plan must go from draft to checked live events
When the product has no tracking yet and you want a first event list, funnels and one main metric
When the client wants one guided run from event plan to a retention grid and dashboard

tasks.task: Plan a test for the biggest drop-off before launch

items.when: When one change is chosen and you need hypothesis, split, main metric, guardrails and stop rule written
Before you commit, to see whether the traffic can prove the lift and how many weeks it needs
When the idea is still loose and you want a second hypothesis and sample size to compare
When there are many ideas, to rank them by impact and risk and test the top one first
When the client wants the leak found, the fix tested and the result read in one run
When the test idea is a guess with no user evidence behind it

tasks.task: Read a finished test and make the ship call

items.when: When the test has ended and you need a split check, the lift as a range and a ship call
When something else happened during the test, to pass or fail each trust check and guardrail
When you are unsure which statistical test fits the metric and whether the result is real
When the client runs tests often and wants each one checked at start and end, with the lesson saved
When a small lift is being told as a certain win and the range needs plain words

tasks.task: Work out churn rate and time to cancel by group

items.when: When you need churn by plan, channel or start month with the counting rule stated
When the client sells subscriptions, to score where subscribers leave
When churn must sit beside recurring revenue and active subscriber counts
When cancel notes or survey answers exist, to turn them into counted themes

tasks.task: Build a repeat purchase view for an online shop

items.when: When you have order dates and want a grid of who orders again, by first-order month
When you need repeat rate and revenue for each first-purchase month
When the owner asks which products bring buyers back within a set number of days
When repeat orders are weak, to find the one stage between first and second order to fix
When the owner asks if repeat orders pay back what a new customer costs

tasks.task: Run the weekly funnel and retention review

items.when: Each week on the same day, using the last complete week
When the client wants the losing step, the likely cause and one experiment named every week
When the numbers are in and you need what moved against target written up
When one number moved sharply, to confirm it is real before anyone reacts

tasks.task: Define the main metric and how each number is counted

items.when: When the team has no agreed main metric, to get one with the numbers that feed it
When you need the right metrics for the product's stage before you define any
When two people count the same metric two ways and one written rule is needed
When the report is full of totals that only go up, to swap them for per-customer numbers
When two regular reports disagree and you must show where the definitions split

tasks.task: Clean up a messy event list or move to a new tool

items.when: When the event list has duplicates, mixed case and values in names, to get one clean set and a map
When the clean list needs properties, owners and a version note so it stays clean
When the list keeps drifting, to find broken tracking and double counts each month

tasks.task: Check new events fire correctly after a release

items.when: When new or renamed events went live, to check each fires once with the right properties
When the release is part of a larger tracking change with sign-off points
When the analytics tool and the database give different counts, to find the step where they split

tasks.task: Check a tracking plan collects no more personal data than needed

items.when: Before a plan goes live or when you inherit one, to find properties the questions do not need
When users are in the EU or California, to list the duties that apply and the proof missing

tasks.task: Find the early action that predicts who stays

items.when: When you can compare what kept and lost customers did early, to set one sign with a time limit
When users leave in week one, to name the cause before you pick a fix
When the sign is set, to get ways to bring new users to it faster
When nobody can say what users would miss if the product went away

tasks.task: Plan or build a product dashboard

items.when: Before any chart, to set who reads it, what they decide and the few metrics that fit
When the client has no analytics tool and needs a dashboard file built from an export
When one finding needs a clean chart with the right chart type
When charts are drafted, to check the chart type and axes do not mislead
When a chart looks tidy but a reader could take the wrong point from it
When the team wants a shared report they can rerun on company data

tasks.task: Analyse a CSV export and report the findings

items.when: When the request is vague, to pin down the question, the decision and the data needed
When the file is new to you, to map its columns, spread and odd spots first
Before any sums, to count gaps, duplicates and odd values in the export
When the export has wrong types, duplicates or outliers that must be fixed and logged
When the file is clean and you need the question answered with trends and tests
Before the findings go out, to check the method, the sums and any bias
When the client wants to ask follow-up questions of the file themselves

tasks.task: Group customers by behaviour or value

items.when: When you have orders and want each customer scored on recency, frequency and spend
When fixed rules miss the pattern, to find natural groups from behaviour
When the client wants accounts at risk of leaving scored from usage and support data
When two groups look different, to test whether the gap is more than chance

tasks.task: Investigate why a metric dropped

items.when: When a number moved, to confirm the change, split it by group and rank the drivers
When the drop shows in one report and not another, to rule out a counting change
When heatmaps or session recordings exist, to see the friction behind the number
When you suspect the drop is broken tracking and not user behaviour

tasks.task: Report recurring revenue, lifetime value and payback

items.when: When you have customer and revenue data and need cohorts, lifetime value and payback worked out
When the numbers are done, to read them against stage and say what to fix first

tasks.task: Write and check SQL for funnel, cohort and test queries

items.when: When the data sits in a database and you need joins, windows and step logic written
When you inherit a query, to see what it counts and which rows it keeps
Before you trust a result, to catch join errors that double count users

tasks.task: Size the fixes and pick what to work on first

items.when: When a fix is proposed, to give a low, base and high gain with each assumption listed
When the team argues over where to work, to name the one limit and the work order
When the plan is a big build and the riskiest guess has not been tested

tasks.task: Turn churn findings into a retention and win-back plan

items.when: When you have cancel reasons, to set one save per reason and the numbers to track
When the plan needs a cancel flow, save offers and failed-payment recovery to choose from
When lapsed buyers should get messages timed to how they really reorder
When the plan's first change should be tested, not just shipped

tasks.task: Write up findings an owner can read in a minute

items.when: When the analysis is long, to put the answer, the impact in numbers and the decision on one page
When one chart would carry the point better than a table
Before you send it, to check each claim follows from the numbers shown

always.when: Before any analysis, to fix the question, the decision it feeds and what data is needed
Before any sums on an export, to count gaps, duplicates and odd values
Before any finding is shared, to check the method, the sums and any bias

helpers.when: When events must be piped into a warehouse or a broken feed must be repaired
When the losing step needs a new page or flow designed, not only a test plan
When the retention plan needs onboarding, save and win-back messages written
When the numbers show where users leave and interviews must show why
When the dashboard needs more than a plan: a designed set of charts for a wide audience
When findings must become a ranked roadmap with owners

gaps: No tool guide covers GA4, Mixpanel, Amplitude or PostHog: how to build a funnel or retention report in each

No library item checks an analytics tracking plan for personal data in properties, consent mode or retention settings
No library item measures time to cancel as a survival curve by group
No library item analyses feature adoption: which features retained users use and lost users do not
No library item reads user paths or sequences to show what users do just before they leave
No library item covers guardrail metrics, peeking and stopping rules for tests in one place
